phrases.phrase: take it with a pinch of salt

model: I'd like to talk about a trip I took to a famous flower garden in the mountains about three years ago. Before I went, I'd seen hundreds of picture-perfect photos on social media, with endless fields of bright flowers and a romantic wooden bridge over a lake, so I was really excited. Unfortunately, it didn't live up to expectations at all. When we arrived, there were only a few small flower beds, and most of the flowers were already dying because we'd gone at the wrong time of year. The lake was much smaller and dirtier than in the photos, and the famous bridge was surrounded by stalls selling souvenirs and plastic hats. There were also far more people than I'd imagined, so it was nearly impossible to take a photo without strangers in it. Basically it was a tourist trap, and the entrance fee was more expensive than anywhere else we visited on that trip. I realised that most of those images were heavily edited photos. Honestly, it was a bit of a let-down. However, it turned out to be a blessing in disguise, because we left early and drove to a small village nearby, where there was a quiet waterfall and a family-run restaurant with the best grilled pork I've ever had. Now, whenever a place looks amazing online, I take it with a pinch of salt.
